case.title: Mr. Okoh Ubeh & Ors v. Board of Management, Federal Medical Centre, Makurdi & Ors
defendants: Board of Management, Federal Medical Centre, Makurdi
The Medical Director, Federal Medical Centre, Makurdi

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Writ of Summons filed at the Federal High Court, Makurdi Division, subsequently transferred to the National Industrial Court by Order dated 19th March 2012.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Trial completed; written addresses filed and adopted; judgment delivered.
orders_before_trial: Order of the Federal High Court, Makurdi Division, dated 19th March 2012 transferring the suit to the National Industrial Court.
procedural_events: Claimants called witnesses and tendered documents.
1st and 2nd Defendants called one witness and tendered documents.
3rd Defendant filed Statement of Defence but called no witness.
Written addresses filed, exchanged, and adopted.

material_facts: Claimants were employees of the Federal Medical Centre, Makurdi.
1st Claimant was a Senior Typist in Administration Department.
2nd Claimant was a Chief Clerical Officer in Administration Department.
4th Claimant worked in Finance and Accounting Department.
Claimants' appointments were terminated vide letters dated 24th September 2010 (1st, 2nd, 3rd Claimants) and 4th February 2010 (4th Claimant).
Prior to termination, there were allegations, queries, replies, and appearance before a Disciplinary Committee.
Termination letters stated 'Service no longer required'.
3rd Defendant claimed termination was based on Federal Government directive on harmonization of fringe benefits vide circular Ref: HCFS/SW/HM/H.021/S.27 dated 11th November 2003, disengaging drivers.

chronology.event: Federal Government circular on harmonization of fringe benefits issued.
Federal High Court ordered transfer of suit to National Industrial Court.

admitted_facts: Claimants were employees of the Federal Medical Centre, Makurdi.
4th Claimant was a staff prior to termination.
disputed_facts: Whether termination was in compliance with Public Service Rules.
Whether termination was actuated by malice.
Whether termination was connected to disciplinary proceedings.
Whether 'Service no longer required' is a valid ground for termination.
background_facts: Claimants held various positions at Federal Medical Centre, Makurdi.
facts.employment_relationship: Employment with statutory flavour governed by Public Service Rules and Guidelines of the Federal Civil Service.
documentary_evidence: Minutes of meetings of 1st Defendant dated 16/9/10 and 29/1/10
witness_evidence: Claimants' witnesses testified and tendered documents.
1st and 2nd Defendants' sole witness testified and tendered documents.

claims.claim: Declaration that termination on grounds of 'Service no longer required' is victimizing, without due process, and lacking basis.
Declaration that termination is null and void.
Declaration that Claimants are still in employment and entitled to salaries and allowances.
General damages for wrongful termination, blackmail, and trauma.

reliefs_sought.relief: Declaration that termination on grounds of 'Service no longer required' is victimizing, without due process, and lacking basis.
Declaration that termination is null and void.
Declaration that Claimants are still in employment and entitled to salaries and allowances.
General damages for wrongful termination, blackmail, and trauma.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether the appointment of the claimants is one of statutory flavour.
Whether the termination of Claimants' appointment is in violation of the relevant statute and the principle of natural justice.

questions_of_law: Whether employment is with statutory flavour.
Whether termination complied with Public Service Rules.

claimant_arguments: Employment is with statutory flavour, governed by Public Service Rules.
Termination on grounds of 'Service no longer required' is not provided for in Public Service Rules.
Termination was actuated by malice and witch-hunting.
Violation of fair hearing as Claimants were not given opportunity to defend.
Claimants proved their case on balance of probabilities.
defendant_arguments: Employment is regulated by statute; termination on notice is valid under Public Service Rules.
Termination is different from dismissal; termination affords right to determine contract at any time.
Claimants failed to prove breach of Public Service Rules.
Defendants not under duty to prove termination is lawful.
3rd Defendant: termination based on Federal Government directive on harmonization of fringe benefits.

evidential_findings.finding: Termination not in compliance with Public Service Rules.

findings_of_fact.finding: Employment is with statutory flavour governed by Public Service Rules.
Termination was not in conformity with Public Service Rules.

findings_of_law.finding: Employment governed by statute is with statutory flavour.
Termination on grounds of 'Service no longer required' is unlawful, null and void.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court found that the employment of the Claimants is with statutory flavour, governed by the Public Service Rules. The termination on grounds of 'Service no longer required' was not in compliance with the Rules, as the Claimants were not given fair hearing and the ground is not provided for in the Rules. Therefore, the termination is unlawful, null and void.

arguments.claimant: Employment is with statutory flavour, governed by Public Service Rules.
arguments.defendant: Employment is regulated by statute; termination on notice is valid.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court examined the appointment letters and Public Service Rules, concluding that the employment is with statutory flavour.
issue_analysis.holding: The appointment is one of statutory flavour.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: Where appointment and termination are governed by statutory provisions, the employment has statutory flavour.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the termination of Claimants' appointment is in violation of the relevant statute and the principle of natural justice.

arguments.claimant: Termination was actuated by malice and violated Public Service Rules and fair hearing.
arguments.defendant: Termination was in compliance with Public Service Rules.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that the termination was not in conformity with the Public Service Rules, as the Claimants were dismissed on grounds of 'Services No Longer Required' without fair hearing.
issue_analysis.holding: The termination is unlawful, null and void.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: Termination of statutory employment must comply with the governing statute and principles of natural justice; failure renders it null and void.
